payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_scheduler.py::test_a_stack_order_stacks_on_an_earlier_batchs_pushed_pull_request stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'The stack base is set only on the specs whose `depends_on` names it.' applied to saffron/scheduler.py as an edit. The claim was "Under `stack=True`, `build_queue` takes a spec whose `depends_on` names a parent outside the order and off the default branch, when that parent's newest task in a `DEPENDENCY_WAITING_STATES` state records a branch, a resolved pushed sha and a pull request URL. That parent is the stack base, and its `StackBase` names that newest waiting task. Every spec of the order carries the stack base. A parent whose push landed is on the default branch, and then no spec carries a stack base. The witness drives each of the three waiting states. It puts an older waiting task with no push and a newer `EXHAUSTED` task beside the stack base's own.", and only that witness ran under the edit.
